reader.requirement: At --std 85 an I-O status 9x is set only for an implementor-defined unsuccessful condition that none of the 1985 status values 00 through 49 describes, and a condition the edition does define keeps its own value (never 9x).

edition-consulted.switches: DialectBehavior.LinageViolatingOpenLeavesFileOpen: at 85 a LINAGE value violation refuses the OPEN with 90 and the file is not open, so a later WRITE/CLOSE answers the 1985 48/42 rather than 90
SharingFacilityInEffect (DialectBehavior.FileSharingFacility): at 85 a host sharing refusal answers 30, never the 2002 status 61 the 1985 list lacks
SharingFacilityInEffect: no run-unit file lock and no 61 at 85

reader.edition-search: grep of FileStatusCode 9x constants and their callers; grep DialectBehavior/SharingFacilityInEffect on the OPEN and WRITE paths
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: at 85 the 90 OPEN leaves the file not open (later statements 48/42/41 per the 1985 list); from 2002 the OPEN succeeds into a broken page and later WRITEs repeat 90. The 9x values themselves (90 LINAGE, 91 character without byte image) are the same at every edition.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: LINAGE 90 and CODE-SET 91 on sequential files; not exercised: 91 on a sequential file with no CODE-SET and on a relative file, and the refusal of line sequential (the 71/06/09 organization) at 85

probes.printed: USE 91 00 / SQ-W=91 / SQ-W2=00 / USE 00 91 / RL-W=91 / SQ-R=00 ABC / EOF / SQ-R2=10
probes.expected: a WRITE of a character with no byte image is an implementor-defined unsuccessful condition (none of 00-49 describes it): 9x, USE runs, nothing reaches the medium, next WRITE 00

probes.printed: relative WRITE RL-W=91 with USE run
EXPECT: MATCH (OPEN 90, second OPEN 90 not 41, WRITE 48 not 90, CLOSE 42)
probes.expected: 9x must not duplicate 4x: the not-open file's WRITE is 48, CLOSE 42

probes.printed: COBOL0900: ORGANIZATION LINE SEQUENTIAL requires COBOL-2023 (targeting COBOL-85)
probes.expected: a later edition's organization (whose 06/09/71 statuses 1985 lacks) is refused at 85

citations.check: OK  §1985:VII.1.3.5 GRL2.5  (1.3.5 I-O Status)  the text is in GRL2.5
OK  §1985:VII.1.3.5 GR5  (1.3.5 I-O Status)  the text is in GR5

reader.notes: The runtime defines exactly two 9x values (90 LINAGE value violation, 91 character with no byte image) and neither condition is one the 1985 00-49 list names. Conditions the 1985 list does name keep their values (48/42/41 after a refused OPEN). At 85 the sharing-refusal 61 is replaced by 30 and line sequential is refused, so no non-1985 status leaks.

refuter.evidence: Read 1985 VII.1.3.5 whole (00/04/05/07, 10, 30/34/35/37/38/39, 41-49): none names a LINAGE value violation (VII.3.7.4 GR2/GR3 only say 'The value must be greater than zero', no status) or a character with no byte image. grep of src for "9[0-9]" finds only FileStatusCode.LinageValueViolation '90' and CharacterWithoutByteImage '91' (MessageStore's 91-93 are communication statuses, not I-O). Probe refute-1985-232/r1_9x.cob at --std 85 (runs/r1_9x-001): LINAGE data-name PG set to 0 then WRITE AFTER ADVANCING PAGE -> USE ran, 90; FOOTING 9 > PG 5 then WRITE ADVANCING PAGE -> 90; relative REWRITE of 'X€Y' -> USE ran, 91, then READ gives 00 ABC (medium unchanged); indexed WRITE of a no-byte-image character -> 91, the next WRITE of the same key 00 (nothing stored). No 9x was produced for a condition the 1985 list names, and the reader's 48/42 after a refused OPEN stands. cite.py: 'OK  §1985:VII.1.3.5 GRL2.5  (1.3.5 I-O Status)  the text is in GRL2.5'; 'OK  §1985:VII.3.7.4 GR2  (║3.7.4 General Rules║)  the text is in GR2'.
